subject: Immunology
vignette: A 34-year-old woman is vaccinated with an mRNA vaccine into the deltoid muscle. Two weeks later she has high titers of neutralizing antibodies and circulating CD8+ T cells specific for the encoded antigen, despite the antigen never being delivered to the cytosol in large amounts clinically.
question: Which dendritic cell process most explains the generation of CD8+ T-cell responses to an exogenous vaccine antigen?

options.text: Cross-presentation of exogenous antigen on MHC class I
Direct loading of antigen onto MHC class II of naive CD8+ T cells
Presentation of antigen by MHC class III molecules
Presentation of lipid antigen by CD1d to NK cells
Transfer of MHC class II from dendritic cells to T cells

explanation_correct: Dendritic cells are the only professional antigen-presenting cells that can cross-present exogenous antigen onto MHC class I to prime naive CD8+ T cells, a process especially characteristic of the CD8alpha+ cDC1 subset. After migrating from the injection site to the draining lymph node, they deliver antigen and costimulation, allowing clonal expansion of cytotoxic T cells. This property is central to vaccines and to tumor immunotherapy.

explanation_incorrect.B: Naive CD8+ T cells do not recognize MHC class II, and peptide loading on class II stimulates CD4+ helpers rather than CD8 effectors.
explanation_incorrect.C: MHC class III molecules encode complement proteins and do not present peptide antigen.
explanation_incorrect.D: CD1d presents lipid antigens to NKT cells, which does not explain antigen-specific CD8+ cytotoxic responses.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dendritic cells do not transfer MHC molecules to T cells as a means of antigen presentation; T cells must recognize MHC on the presenting cell.

educationalObjective: Cross-presentation allows dendritic cells to prime CD8+ cytotoxic T cells against exogenous antigens, a key mechanism for antiviral vaccines and tumor immunity.

subject: Immunology
vignette: A 27-year-old veterinary technician accidentally receives a small unintentional needle inoculation of live vaccinia virus into the skin of the thumb. She has never been vaccinated against smallpox. Within a week a draining axillary node becomes tender, and she develops neutralizing antibody and virus-specific CD8+ T cells.
question: Which cell most likely transported intact vaccinia antigen from the skin to the draining lymph node to initiate this response?

options.text: Neutrophil migrating from the blood into the dermis
Langerhans cell acting as a migratory dermal dendritic cell
Mast cell resident in subcutaneous fat

explanation_correct: Langerhans cells (CD1a+, Birbeck granules) are epithelial dendritic cells that capture antigen in the epidermis and migrate via lymphatics to the paracortical T-cell zone of the draining node, where they present and costimulate naive T cells. This migration converts them from antigen-capturing cells with abundant MHC class II into efficient stimulators of naive T cells. The resulting node enlargement reflects the clonal expansion of antigen-specific lymphocytes.

explanation_incorrect.A: Neutrophils phagocytose and kill organisms but are short-lived and do not migrate to lymph nodes to prime naive T cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: High endothelial venules are specialized vessels allowing lymphocyte entry, not antigen-transporting cells.
explanation_incorrect.D: Plasma cells are antibody-secreting end-stage B cells found in marrow and mucosal tissues, not migratory antigen carriers.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mast cells release histamine and mediators and reside in connective tissue but do not traffic antigen to lymph nodes.

educationalObjective: Langerhans cells are migratory epidermal dendritic cells that carry antigen to draining lymph nodes and are the professional APCs that initiate primary T-cell responses in skin.

subject: Immunology
vignette: A 61-year-old man with metastatic melanoma is treated with intravesical BCG for bladder carcinoma in situ after failing standard therapy. Three weeks later his bladder biopsies show dense mononuclear infiltrates and a CD8+ T-cell rich peritumoral immune response.
question: Which property of dendritic cells is most responsible for converting BCG exposure into detectable antitumor T-cell activation?

options.text: Their capacity to directly kill tumor cells with perforin
Their secretion of IgE in response to BCG
Their delivery of high-level costimulation and pro-inflammatory cytokines along with antigen
Their role as the primary complement-producing cells of the immune system
Their ability to generate antibody by producing surface immunoglobulin

explanation_correct: Dendritic cells mature after encountering pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as BCG cell wall components, increasing costimulatory molecules (CD80/CD86, CD40) and secreting IL-12 that polarizes Th1 and CD8 responses. Without this maturation signal, antigen presentation by immature dendritic cells would render T cells tolerant rather than activated. This is the basis of BCG intravesical therapy, in which robust local inflammation recruits effector cells that clear tumor.

explanation_incorrect.A: Dendritic cells are not primary cytolytic effectors; perforin-mediated killing is carried out by CD8+ T cells and NK cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: IgE is produced by plasma cells and is not the mechanism of dendritic antigen presentation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hepatocytes are the main source of serum complement proteins, not dendritic cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dendritic cells lack surface immunoglobulin and do not secrete antibody.

educationalObjective: Mature dendritic cells provide antigen together with costimulation and IL-12, and this maturation signal is what determines whether T cells become activated or tolerant.
